source_refs.title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Connect a storage device to your Mac
source_refs.applicability: Mac; drive guidance from the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Use a storage device with at least twice the storage capacity of your Mac.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Plug an external drive into a compatible port. Choose one with at least twice your Mac's storage, and use it only for backups.

source_refs.title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Set up the storage device as your backup disk
source_refs.applicability: macOS Ventura 13 or later (the page gives these steps for that version)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Select your connected storage device, then click Set Up Disk.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac with macOS Ventura 13 or later: From the Apple menu, choose System Settings. Click General in the sidebar, then click Time Machine on the right. Click Add Backup Disk, or click the Add button. Select your connected storage device, then click Set Up Disk.

source_refs.title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Set up the storage device as your backup disk (setup prompts)
source_refs.applicability: Mac; prompts that appear during setup
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Either erase it or select a different backup disk or volume.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: If your Mac asks to erase the storage device so that it can be used for Time Machine, either erase it or select a different backup disk or volume. If your Mac asks whether this computer should claim existing backups created on a different computer, claim them if you want them to become part of the backups for this Mac. If you turn on Encrypt Backup to help secure your backup from unauthorized access, you are asked to create a backup password. You will need it if you later restore files from the backup.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps paraphrased from the named section; excerpt quoted exactly

source_refs.title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine - Apple Support
source_refs.applicability: Mac; Time Machine menu bar icon
source_refs.verified_excerpt: choose Back Up Now from the Time Machine menu in the menu bar.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Choose Back Up Now from the Time Machine menu in the menu bar. Or wait for the next automatic backup. The menu shows how much of the current backup is done, or the date and time of the latest backup.

source_refs.title: Back up your Mac with Time Machine - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Learn about backup frequency and duration
source_refs.applicability: macOS Ventura 13 or later (the page gives these steps for that version)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Click Options, then choose a setting from the Back up frequency menu.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac with macOS Ventura 13 or later: To change the backup frequency, choose Open Time Machine Settings from the Time Machine menu. Click Options, then choose a setting from the Back up frequency menu.
